feasibility.verdict: Partially feasible: ELM single-column can mechanistically simulate soil-water infiltration and deep drainage (a recharge proxy), but a defensible 2050 projection requires downscaled/bias-corrected future climate forcing, which is NOT part of the standard GSWP3/CLMNCEP dataset. A present-day baseline plus a delta-perturbed warming run is provided; true recharge magnitudes should be validated against basin observations.
answerable: Baseline present-day recharge (deep drainage QDRAI + gravity drainage QCHARGE) across the Naches elevation gradient
Direction and relative change of recharge under a prescribed warming (delta-temperature) scenario
Shift in recharge seasonality driven by earlier snowmelt (rain-vs-snow partitioning, snowmelt timing)
Sensitivity of soil moisture, infiltration, and drainage to warming by soil texture and elevation
not_answerable: Absolute basin-integrated recharge volume (single-column, no lateral groundwater flow or aquifer storage)
A specific bias-corrected CMIP6 SSP scenario recharge value without externally supplied downscaled forcing
Precipitation-change effects unless a future precip perturbation is prescribed (delta approach here perturbs temperature only)
Managed diversion/irrigation return-flow recharge (regulated Yakima/Naches irrigation system not represented)

parsed.n_justification: The Naches basin is strongly elevation-controlled: recharge is dominated by snowmelt timing at high elevation and by rain infiltration in the valley. Three columns span the hydrologic gradient (snow-dominated headwaters, transitional mixed rain-snow forest, and rain-dominated valley), enough to capture divergent responses of recharge to warming without over-fitting a single-column framework.
requires_capabilities: Present-day GSWP3/CLMNCEP atmospheric forcing (1991-2020) for baseline

Delta-change forcing capability: apply +2 to +3 K air-temperature offset (with optional derived humidity/longwave adjustment) to represent ~2050 mid-century warming; ideally replace with bias-corrected downscaled CMIP6 SSP2-4.5/SSP5-8.5 forcing when available
ELM soil hydrology with unsaturated flow and gravity/aquifer drainage (QCHARGE/ZWT) enabled
Snow model active for snowmelt-recharge partitioning
Spin-up to hydrologic equilibrium prior to analysis period
Optional PFLOTRAN coupling for detailed variably-saturated subsurface flow / recharge to water table
assumptions: Deep drainage flux (QDRAI) plus gravity drainage (QCHARGE) is used as the recharge proxy at the column base
Warming scenario implemented as a temperature-delta perturbation of historical forcing; precipitation held at historical distribution unless downscaled projections are supplied
'By 2050' interpreted as a ~2036-2050 mid-century climatology compared against a 1991-2020 baseline; a matched-length perturbed run is required
Single-column columns represent point vertical fluxes, not lateral or basin-integrated groundwater flow
Irrigation, diversions, and managed reservoir operations in the Naches system are excluded
Model spun up (typically >100 yr accelerated / recycled forcing) before the 30-yr analysis window
